entry.title: How I Think About Reliability in LLM Applications
entry.summary: A lot of people evaluate LLM applications by asking one question: “Does it give a good answer?” That matters, of course. But once you start shipping LLM-powered features to real users, a different question becomes much more important: “Can this system be trusted to behave well over time?” That is how I think about reliability in LLM applications. Reliability is not just about uptime. It is not just about whether the model provider is available. And it is definitely not just about whether the prompt worked on your favorite test case. Reliability is about whether the full system can consistently produce useful outcomes in the messy conditions of real product usage.
